name: Nullframe ChromeSync Interface Gauntlet
description: A precision-machined half-glove in brushed titanium-alloy and soft-grain synthetic leather, covering the back of the hand and wrist while leaving the palm open. Sixteen micro-contact pads are embedded in a lattice across the back panel, each corresponding to standard chrome hand data-port positions across the three most common aug manufacturers. The leather portion is dark oxblood with subtle embossed circuit-trace patterning. A low-profile magnetic clasp locks the unit to chrome forearm flanges.
functionality: Sixteen-point micro-contact pad array interfaces with chrome hand data ports for BCI passthrough, haptic feedback routing, and aug diagnostics. Magnetic flange lock for secure chrome attachment. Open palm preserves tactile function. Compatible with Nullframe, Kestrel, and Axiom chrome standards.
what_it_says: Your augmentation is expensive, maintained, and you want people to know both.
story_hooks: A gauntlet recovered from a Tier 5 boardroom has a hidden passive data-skimmer embedded in one of the micro-contact pads — someone was recording every handshake.
A Tier 3 worker saved for two years to buy one secondhand; it only partially interfaces with her off-brand chrome, but wearing it gets her past the door at Tier 4 networking events.
Nullframe has issued a silent recall on a batch — the magnetic clasp can generate a field that corrupts chrome motor-control firmware, but they don't want to admit how many units are out there.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, asymmetrical half-glove that reads as high-tech minimalism—industrial and precise. The brushed titanium back catches light in subtle gradations, while the oxblood leather wraps the wrist in a sophisticated accent. Worn open-palm, it signals someone who interfaces directly with augmented systems. The lattice of micro-contact pads creates a technical constellation across the back of the hand.
physical_description.fit: Precision-fitted to the back of the hand and wrist; the open palm allows direct contact with chrome interfaces. Compression-style wrist closure with magnetic lock-points for secure fastening to forearm augmentation flanges. Form-hugging but not restrictive.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium-alloy frame with soft-grain synthetic leather (oxblood). Composite lattice backing with embedded micro-contact pads.
physical_description.texture: Titanium is cool and matte with fine brushed finish; leather is supple with subtle embossed circuit-trace detailing that catches fingers when touched. Pads are slightly raised, almost imperceptible to casual touch.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted brushed silver-gray titanium with deep oxblood leather. Embossed circuit traces in barely-visible darker burgundy. Micro-contacts are gunmetal gray with faint luminescent calibration marks.
physical_description.closures: Low-profile magnetic clasp system designed to lock onto standard chrome forearm flanges. No traditional buckles or zippers—interface-first design.
distinctive_features: Sixteen micro-contact pads arranged in lattice pattern across back panel
Embossed circuit-trace patterning on leather—functional aesthetic
Open-palm design for direct skin-to-chrome interface contact
Nullframe Systems branding (minimal, laser-etched on inner wrist)
Magnetic lock-points perfectly calibrated for common aug manufacturers
Lattice backing provides structural rigidity while remaining lightweight
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury. This is specialized corpo or independent operator gear—expensive, precision-engineered, built for someone with serious chrome augmentations.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is either a corporate data-broker, freelance netrunner, or high-tier independent tech operative. Signals someone who interfaces with augmented systems daily and can afford bespoke, manufacturer-agnostic hardware. Not street-level; this is professional-grade.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or lightly broken-in. The design is meant to show no wear—scratches on titanium are minimized through finish quality, leather ages gracefully. Even weathered examples maintain their precision aesthetic.

The brushed titanium back panel glows subtly under moody blue-tinted studio lighting, micro-contact pads catching thin highlights. Oxblood leather wraps the wrist with visible embossed circuit traces. The model's hand shows visible chrome augmentation flanges on the forearm, magnetic lock-points engaged.
